title: Does my setup pass its health check?
summary: Use a recorded flight—and any setup evidence available with it—to review the aircraft, flight controller, logging, power, and health findings before tuning.
questions: What does this recording actually show about my aircraft and flight-controller setup?
Do the recorded values, aircraft details, and available configuration agree?
Which checks found something, and which could not run?

blocks.text: A health check needs evidence. In Airframe, a recorded flight is the examination record, while the aircraft and its flight-controller setup are the patient. Overview brings together what the log recorded, what the Airframe document knows about the aircraft, any configuration captured from the flight controller, and the checks those inputs can support.

steps: Open a Betaflight log or Airframe document and select a representative segment.
Read the setup by topic before opening a deeper analysis.

items.title: Recorded evidence
items.text: The Blackbox header and recorded frames provide firmware, hardware, logging, power, flight, GPS, field-availability, and data-quality facts. A plain .bbl or .bfl can supply only what travelled inside that recording.

items.title: Aircraft context
items.text: You can add the aircraft name, propeller size, propeller blade count, and motor layout. Airframe may suggest Blade Count or Motor Layout when the recording contains enough evidence; review and save the values you want to keep with the document.

items.title: Captured FC configuration
items.text: When a matching configuration was captured during flight-controller import, Overview can add settings that are not guaranteed to exist in the log header. Without it, Airframe stays with the recorded evidence.

items.title: Derived findings
items.text: Airframe runs only the checks supported by the available fields and configuration. A check that lacks its required evidence cannot produce a healthy or unhealthy verdict.

items.title: Aircraft
items.text: Confirm the aircraft identity, propeller size, propeller blade count, and motor layout. They provide the physical context needed by craft presentation and applicable aircraft-specific guides or analysis.

items.title: Flight controller and hardware
items.text: Review the Betaflight version, firmware build, board, MCU family, gyro rate, and detected sensors when those facts are present.

items.title: Blackbox and configuration
items.text: Check the logging device, mode, effective rate, loop time, motor protocol, bidirectional DShot, idle setup, and receiver protocol where the log or associated configuration exposes them.

items.title: Power and flight evidence
items.text: Use cell-count context, start and end voltage, used capacity, current, duration, throttle, GPS, modes, and disarms to understand the conditions under which the setup was recorded.

items.title: Checks and warnings
items.text: Look for log defects and gaps, a restrictive logging rate, incomplete CHIRP evidence, a noticeable center-of-gravity estimate, a motor-pole mismatch, candidate motor eRPM dropouts, eRPM data with RPM filtering disabled, or low battery charge at arm. Each row appears only when its prerequisites and reporting gates are met.

blocks.title: Not checked is not healthy
blocks.text: Missing fields or configuration can prevent individual checks from running. Their absence must not be read as a clean bill of health. Overview reports supported evidence; it does not fill gaps with assumptions.

blocks.title: A baseline, not a diagnosis
blocks.text: The health check cannot inspect loose hardware, prove a universal cause, or recommend a complete tune. Use Spectrum for vibration and filter evidence, System Response for control behaviour, and the physical aircraft for anything a log cannot observe.

blocks.title: Cell count is Betaflight context
blocks.text: Overview reports Betaflight's likely effective cell count: a forced configured count is authoritative; otherwise Airframe reproduces firmware-style voltage detection and marks boundary or fallback uncertainty. It is not an independent battery chemistry detector.
